web.title: Summer Olympic Games
web.description:
The [inaugural Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1896_Summer_Olympics) took place in 1896 in [Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens), then part of the [Kingdom of Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Greece), and the most recent was held in [2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics) in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris), France.

The Games have been held in nineteen countries over five continents: four times in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_Olympics) ( [1904](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1904_Summer_Olympics), [1932](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1932_Summer_Olympics), [1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_Summer_Olympics), and [1996](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Summer_Olympics)), three times in [Great Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Britain_at_the_Olympics) ( [1908](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1908_Summer_Olympics), [1948](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Summer_Olympics), and [2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics)) and in [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France_at_the_Olympics) ( [1900](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1900_Summer_Olympics), [1924](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1924_Summer_Olympics), and [2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics)), twice each in [Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greece_at_the_Olympics) ( [1896](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1896_Summer_Olympics) and [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics)), [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany_at_the_Olympics) ( [1936](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1936_Summer_Olympics) and [1972](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Summer_Olympics)), [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia_at_the_Olympics) ( [1956](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1956_Summer_Olympics) and [2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics)), and [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan_at_the_Olympics) ( [1964](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_Summer_Olympics) and [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Olympics)), and once each in [Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweden_at_the_Olympics) ( [1912](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1912_Summer_Olympics)), [Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium_at_the_Olympics) ( [1920](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1920_Summer_Olympics)), the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_at_the_Olympics) ( [1928](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1928_Summer_Olympics)), [Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finland_at_the_Olympics) ( [1952](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1952_Summer_Olympics)), [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy_at_the_Olympics) ( [1960](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1960_Summer_Olympics)), [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_at_the_Olympics) ( [1968](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_Summer_Olympics)), [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada_at_the_Olympics) ( [1976](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976_Summer_Olympics)), [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_Olympics) ( [1980](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Summer_Olympics)), [South Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korea_at_the_Olympics) ( [1988](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Summer_Olympics)), [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain_at_the_Olympics) ( [1992](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics)), [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_at_the_Olympics) ( [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics)), and [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_at_the_Olympics) ( [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics)).

[London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London) and Paris have hosted three times, while [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles), Athens, and [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo) have each hosted twice; Los Angeles will host the Games for the third time in [2028](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2028_Summer_Olympics).

## Hosting
[Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia_at_the_Olympics), [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany_at_the_Olympics), [Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greece_at_the_Olympics) and [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan_at_the_Olympics) have all hosted the Summer Olympics twice (with Australia hosting for the third time in [2032](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2032_Summer_Olympics)). The other countries to have hosted the Summer Olympics are [Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium_at_the_Olympics), [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_at_the_Olympics), [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada_at_the_Olympics), [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_at_the_Olympics), [Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finland_at_the_Olympics), [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy_at_the_Olympics), [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_at_the_Olympics), [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_at_the_Olympics), [South Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korea_at_the_Olympics), [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union_at_the_Olympics), [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain_at_the_Olympics), and [Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweden_at_the_Olympics), with each of these countries having hosted on one occasion.

[Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia) has hosted four times: in Tokyo ( [1964](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_Summer_Olympics) and [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Olympics)), [Seoul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul) ( [1988](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Summer_Olympics)), and [Beijing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing) ( [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics)).

The only two countries in the [Southern Hemisphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Hemisphere) to have hosted have been Australia ( [1956](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1956_Summer_Olympics), [2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics), and again in [2032](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2032_Summer_Olympics)) and Brazil ( [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics)), with [Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africa) having yet to host any Summer Olympics.

## History
### Recent Games
[![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/Drones_durante_a_abertura_das_Olimp%C3%ADadas_de_T%C3%B3quio.jpg/250px-Drones_durante_a_abertura_das_Olimp%C3%ADadas_de_T%C3%B3quio.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Drones_durante_a_abertura_das_Olimp%C3%ADadas_de_T%C3%B3quio.jpg) The [2020 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Olympics) in Tokyo, Japan, had few attendees as a result of excluding public spectators amid the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic).

[Rio de Janeiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro) in Brazil hosted the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics), becoming the first South American city to host the Olympics, the second Olympic host city in Latin America, after [Mexico City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_City) in [1968](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_Summer_Olympics), as well as the third city in the Southern Hemisphere to host the Olympics after Melbourne, Australia, in [1956](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1956_Summer_Olympics) and [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney), Australia, in [2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics).

The [2024 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics) were held in Paris, France, making it the second city after London to host the Summer Olympics three times (the other times being [1900](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1900_Summer_Olympics) and [1924](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1924_Summer_Olympics), marking a centenary since the latter).

### Future Games
The [2028 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2028_Summer_Olympics) will be held in Los Angeles, California, United States, making it the third city (after Paris ( [1900](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1900_Summer_Olympics), [1924](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1924_Summer_Olympics), [2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics)) and London ( [1908](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1908_Summer_Olympics), [1948](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Summer_Olympics), [2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics))) to host the Games three times (the other times being [1932](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1932_Summer_Olympics) and [1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_Summer_Olympics)), with the U.S. hosting the Summer Olympics for the fifth time.

The [2032 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2032_Summer_Olympics) will be held in Brisbane, Australia, which is the third city to host the Games in Australia and the fourth south of the [equator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equator).

web.description:
The last Olympic games were held in both Milan and Cortina, the first to ever be hosted by two cities, in February 2026. Through 2026, there have been 30 [Summer Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympic_Games), held in 23 cities, and 25 [Winter Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winter_Olympic_Games), held in 22 cities. By 2034, eleven cities will have hosted the Olympic Games more than once: Athens ( [1896](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1896_Summer_Olympics) and [2004 Summer # Summer Olympic Games
## News •
| Summer Games | Firsts and Notable Moments | Star Athletes |
|-|-|-|
| [Paris 1900](https://www.britannica.com/event/Paris-1900-Olympic-Games) | The [Paris](https://www.britannica.com/place/Paris) Games saw women competing for the first time, in a limited number of sports—sailing, lawn [tennis](https://www.britannica.com/sports/tennis), and [golf](https://www.britannica.com/sports/golf)—although the women’s events were not officially approved by the [International Olympic Committee](https://www.britannica.com/topic/International-Olympic-Committee) (IOC). Swimming events were held in the [Seine River](https://www.britannica.com/place/Seine-River). | [Margaret Abbott: A Study Break](https://www.britannica.com/biography/A-Study-Break-1367944); [Albert Ayat: The Master](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Albert-Ayat); and [Alvin Kraenzlein: Rivalry Among Teammates](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Alvin-Kraenzlein-Rivalry-Among-Teammates-1936062). |
| [Rio de Janeiro 2016](https://www.britannica.com/event/Rio-de-Janeiro-2016-Olympic-Games) | The event marked the first time that the Olympic Games—either Summer or Winter—were held in [South America](https://www.britannica.com/place/South-America). The Games featured a record 205 participating NOCs, with more than 11,000 athletes competing in 42 sports. The [Rio](https://www.britannica.com/place/Rio-de-Janeiro-Brazil) Olympics also featured the debut of a [Refugee](https://www.britannica.com/topic/refugee) Team made up of 10 athletes from various war-torn countries who had no permanent new home at the start of the Games. | [Caeleb Dressel](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Caeleb-Dressel), [Michael Phelps](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Michael-Phelps), [Neymar](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Neymar), and [Simone Biles](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Simone-Biles). |
| [Tokyo 2020](https://www.britannica.com/event/Tokyo-2020-Olympic-Games) | Officially the Tokyo 2020 Games, the event was actually held in 2021 because of the [COVID-19](https://www.britannica.com/science/COVID-19) pandemic, becoming the first Olympics to be held after the proposed start date. The [pandemic](https://www.britannica.com/science/pandemic) prompted the Japanese Olympic Committee to bar spectators from the city’s sporting venues—a decision that cost the committee more than $800 million in lost ticket sales. | [Lisa Carrington](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Lisa-Carrington), [Neeraj Chopra](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Neeraj-Chopra), Caeleb Dressel, [Shelly-Ann Fraser-Pryce](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Shelly-Ann-Fraser-Pryce), [Yuto Horigome](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Yuto-Horigome), [Rayssa Leal](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Rayssa-Leal), [Katie Ledecky](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Katie-Ledecky), [Suni Lee](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Suni-Lee), [Emma McKeon](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Emma-McKeon), and [Ariarne Titmus](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Ariarne-Titmus). |
| [Paris 2024](https://www.britannica.com/explore/paris-olympics-2024) | The Summer Games returned to Paris for the third time in modern history. With an eye toward sustainability, the 2024 Paris Olympics were the first Games aligned with the goals and recommendations of the [Paris Climate Agreement](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Paris-Agreement-2015). Actions included public transportation access to all venues, reuse of existing buildings and stadiums as venues, and low carbon and eco-friendly new buildings; organizers reported that more than 98 percent of the energy needed to power the Games came from renewable sources. With the slogan “Games Wide Open,” the Paris Games were the first Olympic Games in history to achieve full gender parity. [Breaking](https://www.britannica.com/art/break-dance) had its Olympic debut in 2024. | Simone Biles, Neeraj Chopra, Caeleb Dressel, Yuto Horigome, Rayssa Leal, Katie Ledecky, Suni Lee, [Noah Lyles](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Noah-Lyles), Emma McKeon, [Arshad Nadeem](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Arshad-Nadeem), [Sha’Carri Richardson](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Sha-Carri-Richardson), [Trinity Rodman](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Trinity-Rodman), [Sophia Smith](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Sophia-Smith-footballer), and Ariarne Titmus. |
| Los Angeles 2028 | Los Angeles will join the three-timers club when the Summer Games return to the city in 2028. The Los Angeles organizers—like their Paris 2024 counterparts—have sustainability in mind as they plan an “Energy Positive Games.” |  |
| Brisbane 2032 | The 2032 Summer Games will head to the [Gold Coast](https://www.britannica.com/place/Gold-Coast-Queensland) of [Australia](https://www.britannica.com/place/Australia). Situated in a region steeped in Indigenous history, the Brisbane Games will showcase First Nations cultures, and planning will incorporate the contributions of [Aboriginal](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Australian-Aboriginal) and [Torres Strait Islander](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Torres-Strait-Islander-people) peoples. |  |

# History of United States cities hosting the Olympics
## In 2028, the Summer Olympics will take place in Los Angeles, making it the ninth time that the U.S. has played host
#### By Kelley Ekert •Published August 8, 2021•Updated on March 4, 2024 at 12:46 pm
![](https://media.nbcnewyork.com/2021/07/los-angeles-olympic-cauldron.jpg?quality=85&strip=all&resize=1200%2C675)

NBC Los Angeles

0:00

Pause

Unmute

ShareToggle Fullscreen

NBCUniversal Media, LLC

Which cities in the United States have hosted the Olympics?

[The Beijing Games](https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/beijing-2022) marked the second time that the Chinese city has hosted the Olympics.

Paris is set to takeover as host of [the 2024 Olympics](https://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/sports/2024-paris-olympics-see-dates-sports-how-to-watch-and-more/4926345/). [Milano Cortina](https://milanocortina2026.olympics.com/en/) and [Los Angeles](https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/los-angeles-2028) follow as the winter and summer hosts 2026 and 2028, respectively.

[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyBoZWlnaHQ9IjEyIiB3aWR0aD0iMTcuNjQ3MDU4ODIzNTI5IiB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIvPg==)![Watch button](https://media.nbcnewyork.com/assets/editorial/national/images/cta-eye-icon-white.png)  WATCH HERE](https://www.nbcnewyork.com/watch/?_osource=ed_npd_nbc_ny_site_fast_auto4)

## Which U.S. cities have hosted an Olympics?
In 2028, the Summer Olympics will take place in Los Angeles, making it the ninth time that the U.S. has played host.

**1904 Summer Olympics: St.** **Louis, Missouri**

[2024 Paris Olympics](https://www.nbcnewyork.com/tag/2024-paris-olympics/)

### [Get to know Team USA Olympians ahead of the 2024 Paris Olympics](https://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/sports/team-usa-us-olympians-2024-olympics-paris/4964845/?amp)
**1932 Summer Olympics: Los Angeles, California**

**2028 Summer Olympics: Los Angeles, California**

The 2028 Los Angeles Olympics will run from July 21 to Aug.

## Which country has hosted the most Olympics?
The U.S. and France will both add to their totals with the 2024 Paris Olympics and the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

The 2020 Tokyo Games was Japan’s fourth Olympics, and Italy will tie them for the third-most after the 2026 Milano Cortina Olympics.
